column5: Horizontal privilege escalation: employee B reads employee A's CME record by guessing its id
column8:
HTTP 403 with error_code AUTH_002
the body contains neither A's employee code nor the record title
column12: Ownership is enforced in TrainingAccessPolicy, not only in the query

column5: Vertical privilege escalation: a plain USER calls the admin surface
column7: GET /api/v1/users and GET /api/v1/dashboard/overview with a USER token
column8:
HTTP 403 with error_code AUTH_002 on both
no employee list and no aggregate figures in either body
column12: @PreAuthorize is evaluated by method security, so the handler never runs

column5: Credential exposure: does any response echo a password, and is the stored value hashed?
column6: REST Assured equivalent (JUnit 5 + real HTTP) + direct DB read
column7: POST /api/v1/users (admin creates an account), then GET /api/v1/me
column8:
Neither body contains "password" or a "$2a$" hash
DB: users.password starts with $2a$ (BCrypt)
column12: The generated first-login password travels by email only, never in the HTTP response

column5: Token forgery: edit the JWT payload so roles claims ADMIN, keep the original signature
column7: GET /api/v1/users with a token whose base64url payload was rewritten ("USER" → "ADMIN") and the signature left untouched
column8:
HTTP 401 with an empty body and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
no privilege gain — the request never reaches the controller
column12: Only a real HTTP test can prove this: MockMvc's jwt() post-processor never invokes NimbusJwtDecoder, so signature verification is untested at L1/L2

column5: SQL injection through a filter parameter
column7: GET /api/v1/users?keyword=' OR 1=1--  (URL-encoded) with an ADMIN token
column8:
HTTP 200 with an EMPTY content array — the payload is matched as a literal string
no "SQL" or "Exception" text in the body; the users table is intact
column12: JPA parameter binding; the payload never reaches the SQL grammar

column5: Injection through the Spring Data sort parameter (a classic property-path pivot)
column8: 4xx/5xx without executing anything: no "org.hibernate" or "at vn.vietduc" in the body, and the users row count is unchanged
column12: The sort whitelist (see L3-TRN-02) is what blocks this — endpoints without a whitelist would be worth re-testing

column5: Credential stuffing: 20 consecutive failed logins against one account
column7: POST /api/v1/auth/login × 20 with wrong passwords, then once with the correct password
column8: Every attempt answers the same 400 REQ_001 — and that is the finding: no 423/429, no counter, no delay, and the correct password still works immediately
column12: D38: no rate limiting and no lockout anywhere in the app (only manual PATCH /users/{id}/lock). /auth/forgot-password and /user/first-login/send-email-otp are equally unthrottled

column5: Error hygiene and traceability: does a handled error leak internals, and can a client trace be joined to the server log?
column7: GET /api/v1/training/records/99999999, then the same request with X-Correlation-ID: l3-trace-42
column8:
404 SYS_404 with a correlation id header and no stack trace, class name or SQL fragment in the body
an inbound X-Correlation-ID is echoed unchanged
column12: Caveat: authentication failures bypass this handler entirely, so 401 responses carry no correlation id (D36)

column5: Security misconfiguration: active ZAP scan plus transport hardening (HTTPS redirect, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, CSP)
column7: zap-cli active-scan against the deployed base URL, then inspect the response headers of any endpoint over TLS
column8: No high-risk ZAP alerts; HSTS present; no security-header findings; TLS 1.2+ only
column12: BLOCKED: no ZAP in this environment and the test server speaks plain HTTP, so neither the scan nor the header set can be asserted. The test exists with @Disabled carrying this reason. Also worth checking there: app.cors.allowed-origin-patterns defaults to "*" while allowCredentials(true) — safe in configured environments, dangerous if the property is ever unset
